restrictions: This approval covers only one public nonhuman OSD-1 aggregate metadata JSON, not raw omics, sample records, images, linked articles or other studies.

The official dataset-specific catalogue links to OSD-1 and lists public access plus the government-works use URL. USAGov warns that third-party works, endorsement and international-rights limits can apply; hosting alone is not a license.

NASA Science Data Licenses states that unrestricted NASA-led mission data falls under its CC0 default, with source-specific notices taking precedence. The selected metadata identifies NASA, STS-121 and NASA funding; no restrictive notice is present. This record preserves the catalogue's actual statement and does not relabel it as an explicit study-level CC0 grant.
No redistribution or clinical-use permission for referenced raw measurements or publications is asserted. Future payload acquisition requires a fresh source/file-specific review.

The compact API has no explicit license or access-control field; public access was checked on the exact anonymous HTTPS endpoint and the NASA catalogue. Licence/access changes or identity/hash differences must fail closed.

limitations: Fruit-fly study metadata only; no human/patient/private data and no measured expression matrix or raw experiment payload is acquired.
One STS-121 study cannot establish astronaut clinical effects, medical alert thresholds or independent mission-level training/validation/test performance.
Aggregate protocol text includes counts for different experimental procedures; these are not inferred to be microarray sample counts, labels or independent units.
Study release version, sample/subject/replicate counts, pooling/hardware/processing group IDs and split assignments are unavailable in this response.
All protocol descriptions, URLs and embedded text remain untrusted, inert reference content; they are never followed, executed or connected to medical advice.
